history.period: c. 1990-2002 (about 12 years of construction); inaugurated 1 December 2002
history.summary: NOT A SINGLE TEMPLE - a sprawling 40-acre modern Hindu spiritual/theme park; keep-or-drop decision needed. Built by Brigadier Kapil Mohan (retd), Padma Shri awardee and heir to the Mohan Meakin Limited (Old Monk) brewery family, at a reported cost of about Rs 100 crore; inaugurated by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 1 December 2002. Set on a hillside overlooking the Ashwani Khad valley at Harat (Hart) village, about 15 km north of Solan town (CSV town corrected: Harat, not Solan town; address given as Shakti Sthal / NH-22 between Kalka and Shimla). The complex centres on a large temple-like structure with two big 'Om' symbols at the front and Surya in a seven-horse chariot on top, with artwork of Hindu legends from the Vedas, Ramayana and Mahabharata, life-size statues of famed Vedic rishis and mythological figures, and animal motifs (elephant, lion, tiger, peacock, river dolphin). One vlog claims 108 idols of gods 4-6 ft tall - unverified. The complex also has a Kali Ka Tibba shrine, herbal therapy centres, community kitchens, study centres, open theatres and planned ropeway trolleys; its stated purpose is promoting Vedic sciences and Indian culture among youth.

name: Mohan Shakti National Heritage Park
town_description: Harat (Hart) is a hillside village in Solan district, Himachal Pradesh, about 15 km north of Solan town on the Kalka-Shimla corridor. It overlooks the Ashwani Khad valley and the Shivalik foothills.
tradition: Hinduism (modern Hindu heritage complex; not a single temple)

travel.road: On NH-22 (Kalka-Shimla), at Shakti Sthal / Mandir Road, Hart village, ~15 km north of Solan
